# From a spec to a plan

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

Use this when `spec.md` is accepted. The plan is two files in the spec folder, `plan.md` (how: constraints, approach, files, linter, risks, trace) and `tasks.md` (small tasks you can test one at a time).

## First prompt

```text
/crav1-plan-from-spec
@docs/specs/<slug>/

The spec is accepted. Write plan.md and tasks.md. Do not write code.
```

## Steps

| Step | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Built pieces (partial slices) | For each built piece: finish the gap, add a verify test, or leave it | When the spec is partial or `## In the code` names paths, reads that repo and branch first. A piece that already matches v0 is marked already there and is not a choice. A piece you leave gets one line under `## Left as committed` and no task |
| Plan | When a leftover might be current work or later, answer `current` or `later` in one batch | Writes `plan.md` and `tasks.md`. Each task row names its check before any code: `(verify: <kind> — <named check>) (spec: …)`. Each question you kept open becomes its own entry under Risks. One that blocks some current tasks says `kept open; blocks T2, T4 until resolved.` One that blocks no current task gets `Blocks: none` and does not say "do not implement until resolved". Only a question with no `Blocks:` line keeps that phrase. Stale research findings are listed under Risks and do not block |
| Linter | When the plan says there is no linter for the code the tasks touch: add one, or go on without | `## Linter` names the repo's linter or checker. When there is none, the plan stops before Build until you choose. It does not install one |
| Review (optional) | `/crav1-review-plan` | Starts the `crav1-plan-reviewer-agent` subagent. Numbered findings `P#` in chat. Writes nothing |
| Tighten (optional) | `/crav1-tighten-plan`, then one card: `yes (Recommended)`, or type changes on that card, for example `Retry path (P1) keep` | Patches only the picked issue in `plan.md` or `tasks.md`. Since 1.145.0 the reply prints a findings table (id, issue, options, recommendation) immediately before that card. The card names each item, for example `Tasks miss the 400 path (P4): add a test`. It does not say `table above` unless that table is in the reply. The card is not asked without the table. An item you do not mention keeps its recommendation. There is no Edits choice (1.130.0). A finding about the spec goes back to `/crav1-tighten-spec` |
| Accept | Read `plan.md` and `tasks.md`. Edit them if needed. Say they are accepted | — |

On a `spec/<slug>` branch, do not build. Merge that branch first, then `/crav1-create-feature-branch` to `feat/<slug>`.

## What gets written

- `docs/specs/<slug>/plan.md` and `tasks.md`. `/crav1-plan-from-spec` ends a task line with `(after: T1)` when the task needs an earlier one done first. Optional `(step: 1)` links a task to an Approach step, and optional `(map: feat/cancel-refund)` puts that task on another branch. Leave both off for one branch per step.
- On `spec.md`, `Blocks: T#` under a kept-open question that blocks some of the new tasks, and `Blocks: none` under one that blocks no current task, written by `/crav1-plan-from-spec`. The risk line for `Blocks: T2, T4` is `kept open; blocks T2, T4 until resolved.` When current work blocks the whole slice, the plan writes `- Blocks: whole slice` and the risk line `kept open; blocks the whole slice until resolved.` A `Blocks:` line wins over that Risk wording. Only a question with no line keeps "do not implement until resolved". a missing line holds `T#` ids named in the question, and holds the whole slice only when no task is named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded.
- `/crav1-review-plan`: one `Reviewed: <date>, P# open: <n>` line under the plan title. `<n>` is the `open` value from `plan_check.py open-count --review <file>`. `/crav1-tighten-plan` lowers `<n>` with `reviewed --items`, which counts the items file.
- `/crav1-plan-from-spec` and `/crav1-tighten-plan` print computed output from one script, `scripts/plan_check.py`: the dependency waves (`order`), the plan-from-spec recap and its one Next line (`recap`), the tighten-plan index, counts and empty-queue Next line (`queue`), the findings table with its card (`batch`), and the Reviewed line (`reviewed`). The wording is the same as before. The assistant still picks the findings and their options.
- `/crav1-plan-from-spec`, `/crav1-review-plan` and `/crav1-tighten-plan` end with Run next: a plain label on its own line, then the command alone in its code span, such as `Review the plan, which is written and not reviewed yet:` above `/crav1-review-plan <slug>`. There is no `Next:` line. A spec finding that is already patched, dropped or kept no longer sends you back to `/crav1-tighten-spec`. A `## Linter` section that names a tool, or records going on without one, counts as named even when another line says there is no linter for part of the code.
- Matching OpenSpec export files, only when those already exist.
- Tighten-plan: only the picked issue.

Not written: other `spec.md` lines, application code, any linter install.

## One spec, several branches (1.64.0)

When the spec's work sits on several branches (its `Synced at` lines, its Match `Branch:` list, or task `(branch: …)` parts), `/crav1-plan-from-spec` reads every one of them in the Built pieces step without checking any out, and labels a piece that only exists on an unmerged branch `only on feat/orders-retry, not merged`. A task that finishes or tests such a piece ends with `(branch: feat/orders-retry)`; with the repo too when the spec spans repos (`(branch: orders-api feat/orders-retry)`). Code in another repo is read from `../<repo>`.

`/crav1-tighten-spec` reads the same branches. A yes on "write the branch onto the spec?" adds a `Branch:` line in sorted place instead of replacing the list. A listed branch that is gone and was never merged is offered `(dropped)`; a deleted branch whose work is already in the base is reported as `merged, branch deleted` and isn't offered.

## A yes before something is applied (1.141.0)

A constraint such as `The partner gives a yes before the CI build policy script is applied.` becomes an item under `## Approval needed`, with `Person:` and `Holds:` for the tasks that do that work. `/crav1-plan-from-spec` writes the item. It does not write `Approved:`.

## A wait on another pull request (1.201.1)

A task that should start only after another pull request merges, and that pull request has no task of its own, carries `(after: PR 87)`. When the task text says `after PR 87 merges` and the mark is missing, `plan_check.py order` names the line. On yes, `plan_check.py after-pr --root <spec-folder> --yes` writes the mark.

## Host setup tasks (1.115.0)

A requirement that is a host setting with no file in the repo (a branch policy, required build, reviewers, an approval, a variable group) becomes its own task marked `(host setup)`, verified by reading the live setting back.

## After

See which tasks are ready, any time: `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`.

Reference pages: [plan-from-spec](reference/skills/crav1-plan-from-spec.md) · [review-plan](reference/skills/crav1-review-plan.md) · [tighten-plan](reference/skills/crav1-tighten-plan.md)

The run ends as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says: Run next, never a `Next:` line (1.176.0, 1.177.0), `Waiting:` only when a step is blocked, and `Uncommitted:` when files changed and are not committed.

## Claimed tasks (1.151.0)

A task listed in `docs/specs/<slug>/claims.md` as `In progress:` is left unchanged: no renumber, reorder, rewrite, or removal. After writing `tasks.md`, the plan step preserves those lines and says once which claimed tasks were kept.
